note: The two sets are nearly identical claim-for-claim; the only difference in the shown samples is that Set A additionally captures the 'DOOR FRAME & WALL TRIM FIN. W/ P4' note, a real finish callout on the page that Set B omits. Both sets share the same strengths (the artwork-package note, the two scale callouts, the door/wall dimensions) and the same weaknesses: several dimensions are bound to a non-existent 'Wall section' entity, 8'-8" is attributed to WEST LIVING ELEVATION when it belongs to the WEST BEDROOM ELEVATION, and many claims are vague 'interior elevation | dimension' entries or trivial presence labels. Because the shared claims are identical and A carries one extra correct, non-administrative claim, A is the better set.
remarks: Both extractions invent a 'Wall section' entity for dimensions that actually belong to the individual elevation drawings (13'-3 3/4", 3'-9 11/16", 2'-11 3/16", 1'-6"); these should be bound to the named elevations. 8'-8" and 9'-10 1/4"/9'-2" sit in the WEST BEDROOM and SOUTH BEDROOM elevations respectively, so the WEST LIVING ELEVATION binding for 8'-8" is wrong. The quote '4 1/2" ... W2' splices two separate text runs with an ellipsis and does not support the attribute 'depth'. Facts on the page that neither shown sample captures include D3, TV, MWD01, P3/P4, 3'-6 1/4", 4'-3", 9'-11 1/2", 9'-2 3/4" and 9'-10 1/4" (some may exist in the unshown shared claims). Presence-only claims for WB/P1/P2/F1/F2/MWD02 are of low engineering value.
